title: Google deep-learning DR screening in Thailand's national program: 7,651 patients, specialist-level accuracy
summary: At nine primary-care sites (Dec 2018-Mar 2020) Google's deep-learning system graded fundus photos in real time, 94.7% accuracy for vision-threatening DR, 2,412 referrals; a fifth of images rejected.
account: Ruamviboonsuk et al. (Lancet Digital Health, 7 March 2022), a prospective interventional cohort study funded by Google and Rajavithi Hospital with Google Health co-authors, deployed a deep-learning system at nine primary-care sites of Thailand's national diabetic retinopathy screening program between 12 December 2018 and 29 March 2020. Of 7,940 patients screened, 7,651 were analyzed and 2,412 (31.5%) were referred for retinopathy, macular edema, ungradable images or low acuity; for vision-threatening retinopathy the system's accuracy was 94.7%, sensitivity 91.4% and specificity 95.4%, against 93.5%, 84.8% and 95.5% for retina-specialist over-readers. MIT Technology Review (27 April 2020) reported Google's own field study of the deployment in 11 clinics: more than a fifth of images were rejected, nurses were frustrated by rejections and slow internet, and when it worked the system sped screening. The Nation Thailand (10 February 2025) reported Google and Perceptra planning AI screening for about 1 million people in Thailand over a decade, citing more than 600,000 patients screened with the model globally. The earlier reviewer saw the abstract only and did not enter it to stay within the record cap. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Real-time automated grading of fundus photographs for diabetic retinopathy in a national screening program
system: Google Health deep-learning diabetic retinopathy screening system
deployer: Thailand national diabetic retinopathy screening program (Ministry of Public Health guidelines) with Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok
segment: People with diabetes due for retinopathy screening

ratings.reason: 7,651 patients received real-time grading with specialist-level accuracy and 2,412 were referred.
Real-time results in primary care; field reporting notes speed gains when the system worked and rejections and connectivity problems when it did not.

ai_role.statement: The deep-learning grades and referral recommendations were delivered in real time with specialist over-reading as a safety net; accuracy figures come from the vendor-funded, vendor co-authored prospective study, while an independent news account of Google's field study records substantial image rejection and nurse frustration.

Same Thai community-based national screening program, 4,852 participants and eight non-mydriatic camera types: the deep-learning algorithm showed better sensitivity, specificity and kappa than human graders (Srinivasan et al., Life)

headline: Google DR screening in Thailand matches specialists at 94.7%

comparator.against: regional retina specialist over-readers, measured against an adjudicated reference standard from fellowship-trained retina specialists
comparator.after: an accuracy of 94·7% (95% CI 93·0-96·2), sensitivity of 91·4% (87·1-95·0), and specificity of 95·4% (94·1-96·7)
comparator.quote: For vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy, the deep-learning system had an accuracy of 94·7% (95% CI 93·0-96·2), sensitivity of 91·4% (87·1-95·0), and specificity of 95·4% (94·1-96·7). The retina specialist over-readers had an accuracy of 93·5 (91·7-95·0; p=0·17), a sensitivity of 84·8% (79·4-90·0; p=0·024), and specificity of 95·5% (94·1-96·7; p=0·98).

later.note: A Nature Medicine comment of 23 September 2026 by the Google and partner-site authors describes scaling the same deep-learning screening tool across India, Thailand and Australia; an October 2026 AI Weekly alert summarizing it says the model, ARDA, has now screened more than one million patients, with Perceptra licensed to run screening in Thailand.
later.quote: Scaling a successful deep learning tool across three highly distinct settings – in India, Thailand and Australia — offers cross-cutting insights that may inform the expansion of healthcare artificial intelligence globally.
